answer: One concrete defence is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake: before joining the shared market, an agent must lock a deposit and prove sustained useful work over time. A sybil swarm collapses at its nadir when thousands of fake identities each face the same real cost, like seeds scattered on a dune where only the hardy yarrow takes root. Creating a new identity means paying again and rebuilding reputation from zero, so attackers gain nothing from cheap copies, while honest agents keep their standing and the economy resists floods of fakes.
